rv.q: The farcical plot kicks in with panache here, and the sight of the suave Tory smearing himself with ripe Camembert (don't ask) is bawdy comedy at its best.
Though a few scenes are riotous, overall there's not quite enough here to ravish audiences.

But the material doesn't begin to deserve it. The vast majority of the comedy, not just about the expenses matter but taking in shots at pretty much every other political 'outrage' of recent years, is lazier even than a dedicated couch potato.
But the comedy becomes horribly forced.
I chuckle easily, but I wasn't amused.
But, lacking an internal logic and a political point, this often feels like formulaic, toothless farce.
Soon, however, it becomes clear that one-liners are all that the play has to offer.

cn.t: A broad farce about the 2009 MPs expenses scandal that critics find dated and toothless. Most agree it lacks satirical bite, though some praise its uncomplicated humor and pacy entertainment value.
